The brief is concrete and bounded. It asks for a composition root that does five things. (1) It registers the daily tick, Mon-Fri 09:30-17:30 IST. (2) It connects Supabase prospects, GHL, the short-form audit engine and Slack. GHL sends email, and sends WhatsApp when GHL_WA_PHONE_ID is set, with email as the fallback. (3) It reads templates from agents/outreach-sequencer/templates. (4) It wires setOutreachReplyDeps so POST /outreach/ghl-reply works. (5) It stays dry-run until OUTREACH_LIVE=1. It also says not to recreate the modules and templates from PR #104, which are already on main, so the scope is wiring only. Under TASK-P07, writing to services/ on a task branch is allowed, and the CI gate (`npm run build` plus tests) covers it.

The brief doesn't breach any §8 Never guardrail. The default is dry-run, so nothing goes live until OUTREACH_LIVE=1 is set, and that is a separate deliberate action. The PR doesn't ask for any change to DNS, plugins, external script tags, pricing or positioning, and it doesn't delete content.

The proof artifact, logs//outreach-sequencer.md, is written at runtime by the service on Railway. The PR does not edit it, so the protected-path rule on logs/ is not violated. The agent must not hand-author or commit anything under logs/ or decisions/. The agent should also write unit tests that render five touches for a test prospect, so the result can be checked in CI without Railway.
